title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck is writing down explicit Belyi-type equations for very degenerate 'regular maps' on the sphere: the monogon and the bigon (degenerate dihedra/hosohedra). The base is X_0 = P^1 with marked points 0, 1, ∞; X_1 and X_2 are the covering spheres. This fits the surrounding pages, which tabulate symmetry groups D_5, S_3, (Z/2)^2 and face counts for the icosahedron and dodecahedron, oriented pentagons and so on.

The page opens by saying that if the normalisation of the special points were different, the desired map would just be the squaring z ↦ z^2 of (25). Otherwise one must compose it with homographies.

He takes:
- ψ, the homography 0 ↦ 0, 1 ↦ ∞, ∞ ↦ 1, namely ψ(z) = σ_0(z) = z/(z−1);
- φ, the homography 1 ↦ 0, −1 ↦ ∞, with φ(z) = (z−1)/(z+1). It sends ∞ ↦ 1 and 0 ↦ −1, so 0 and ∞ go to the same point only after squaring.

Composing gives (26):
g_1(z) = ψ(φ(z)^2) = −(1/4)(z−1)^2/z.
This is a degree-2 map P^1 → P^1. It is the quotient by the involution z ↦ 1/z (one checks g_1(1/z) = g_1(z)).
- It is ramified at z = 1 over 0 and at z = −1 over 1, since g_1(−1) = 1.
- The fibre over ∞ is {0, ∞}, unramified.
Its dessin on X_1 is the 'monogone'; he calls it 'équation des monogones, victoire !'.

He then pulls back by z ↦ z^2 to get (27):
g_2(z) = g_1(z^2) = −(1/4)(z^2−1)^2/z^2 = −(1/4)(z − 1/z)^2.
This is a degree-4 Galois cover with group (Z/2)^2, generated by z ↦ −z and z ↦ 1/z. Every ramification index is 2:
- over ∞ at z = 0 and z = ∞;
- over 0 at z = ±1;
- over 1 at z = ±i.
This gives the 'bigône' dessin.

The point is to have explicit normalised coordinates on these degenerate regular-polyhedron covers. They feed the study of Teichmüller groupoids in genus 0 and of the automorphism groups listed on the next page.
errors: The phrase '0 (ou ∞) → 1' is loose. φ(z) = (z−1)/(z+1) sends ∞ to 1 but 0 to −1; only φ^2 sends both 0 and ∞ to 1. The final formula (26) is nevertheless correct.
Otherwise the computations (26) and (27) are correct: −4z/(z+1)^2 is the denominator of ψ(φ^2), and g_1(z^2) simplifies as stated.

ideas.what: Explicit degree-2 Belyi map for the monogon dessin, normalised by composing z ↦ z^2 with homographies: g_1(z) = −(1/4)(z−1)^2/z
ideas.modern_name: Belyi map / dessin d'enfant of a degenerate regular map (quotient of P^1 by an involution)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Schwarz); dessins framework due to Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984), Belyi (1979)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps and dessins in general; this explicit formula is not known to be there

ideas.what: Klein four-group cover g_2(z) = −(1/4)(z − 1/z)^2 as the bigon (dihedral D_2) dessin
ideas.modern_name: Galois Belyi map with group (Z/2)^2; dihedral/hosohedral regular map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder, 1884) for the polyhedral group quotient maps

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine normalisations of classical quotient maps by Z/2 and (Z/2)^2. They are interesting only as a trace of Grothendieck's hands-on computation of regular-map equations around 1978–79, which belongs to the prehistory of dessins d'enfants.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'en lieu étaient' is likely '[si les] lieux étaient' or '...au lieu...'; the opening is hard to read, so this is uncertain.
'bosse' in line 2 is uncertain; it may be 'borne' or similar.
'(25)' refers to the squaring map z ↦ z^2. The inserted phrase reads roughly 'ou de la composition avec une transformation homographique' (insertion and its placement as transcribed are plausible).
'φ(z) = (z−1)/(z+1)' is correct as transcribed, and 'à merveille' in the final line is plausible.
